product.manufacturer: Public GitHub project, used as an external test case

kev.shortDescription: Apache Log4j2 contains a vulnerability where JNDI features do not protect against attacker-controlled JNDI-related endpoints, allowing for remote code execution.
kev.requiredAction: For all affected software assets for which updates exist, the only acceptable remediation actions are: 1) Apply updates; OR 2) remove affected assets from agency networks. Temporary mitigations using one of the measures provided at https://www.cisa.gov/uscert/ed-22-02-apache-log4j-recommended-mitigation-measures are only acceptable until updates are available.
kev.vulnerabilityName: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

signature.title: Log4Shell: JNDI lookup in logged data
signature.provenance: Curated from GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-5v3q and the Apache Log4j security page
signature.fix: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 or later (2.12.4 / 2.3.2 for Java 7 / 6).

decision.rationale: All exploit conditions hold at src/main/java/fr/christophetd/log4shell/vulnerableapp/MainController.java:18. Fix: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 or later (2.12.4 / 2.3.2 for Java 7 / 6).

evidence.desc: Service code logs through the Log4j 2 API
Untrusted request data reaches a logging call
evidence.snippet: logger.info("Received a request for API version " + apiVersion);

evidence.detail: no match in 8 service files; not sufficient on its own. Apache withdrew this flag as a complete mitigation after CVE-2021-45046; upgrade instead.

assessments.title: Incomplete fix for Apache Log4j vulnerability

kev.shortDescription: Apache Log4j2 contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability due to the incomplete fix of CVE-2021-44228, where the Thread Context Lookup Pattern is vulnerable to remote code execution in certain non-default configurations.
kev.vulnerabilityName: Apache Log4j2 Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

signature.title: Log4j incomplete fix: lookups via Thread Context data
signature.provenance: Curated from GHSA-7rjr-3q55-vv33 and the Apache Log4j security page

decision.rationale: No path from untrusted input to the vulnerable behaviour was found. This rests on a heuristic data-flow check, so it needs a reviewer's confirmation. Exploitation also needs a non-default layout that references Thread Context data (for example ${ctx:...}); check log4j2.xml before closing.

evidence.desc: Service code logs through the Log4j 2 API
Untrusted request data written to the Thread Context / MDC
evidence.detail: no call site receives request-derived data (heuristic taint)

assessments.title: Remote Code Execution in Spring Framework

kev.shortDescription: Spring MVC or Spring WebFlux application running on JDK 9+ may be vulnerable to remote code execution (RCE) via data binding.
kev.vulnerabilityName: Spring Framework JDK 9+ Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

signature.title: Spring4Shell: RCE via data binding on JDK 9+
signature.provenance: Curated from GHSA-36p3-wjmg-h94x (exploit prerequisites listed by the Spring team)
signature.fix: Upgrade to Spring Framework 5.3.18 / 5.2.20 or later (Spring Boot 2.6.6 / 2.5.12).

decision.rationale: Exploit prerequisites not met: Runs on JDK 9 or higher is not true here (java_major = 8); Packaged as a WAR is not true here (packaging = jar). The Spring team states the known exploit needs a WAR on Tomcat but the underlying flaw is more general. A not_affected decision here covers the known exploit path only; schedule the upgrade regardless.

evidence.desc: Service defines Spring MVC or WebFlux request handlers
Apache Tomcat is the servlet container
A handler binds request parameters onto a POJO

evidence.detail: no match in 8 service files; not sufficient on its own. The Spring team warns local @InitBinder methods can override a global block; upgrade instead.

decision.rationale: Not listed as known-exploited in the CISA KEV catalogue (2026.09.23). Handle through normal vulnerability management; re-scan picks up new KEV listings.
